summary: Patronus is an Earth system trend detective for hydropower. For 466 river basins that hold 1,053 GW of hydropower, it takes NASA satellite measurements of stored water (GRACE/GRACE-FO), lake levels (G-REALM altimetry) and rainfall (GPCP), plots each series since 2002, and tests the trend with Sen's slope and Mann-Kendall, using false-discovery control. Water storage fell significantly in basins with 392 GW of hydropower. Only 19 GW of that also had less rain, so most of the loss has other causes. Our showpiece is Lake Kariba (Zambia/Zimbabwe). Using only data available at the time, our El Niño water-balance model raised an alarm in July 2023, 5 months before the official cut and 8 months before load-shedding. Today it gives a 36% chance that Kariba falls below 10% usable storage by December 2027. Every forecast is timestamped, and we publish our misses next to the hits.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Patronus shows where the water behind the world's hydropower is changing, and warns when a reservoir is heading for a power shortfall. It answers the challenge directly. The user picks a variable (water storage, lake level, rainfall) and a region (any hydropower basin or reservoir). Patronus plots the time series since 2002 and measures the rate of change (Sen's slope) and whether it is significant (Mann-Kendall with the Hamed-Rao autocorrelation correction, Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery control across basins). The Trend Detective page lets anyone do this themselves.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Regions: each hydro plant in the WRI Global Power Plant Database is placed in a HydroBASINS level-4 basin, giving 466 basins with 1,053 GW.

2. Trends: monthly GRACE/GRACE-FO water storage (Apr 2002 to Aug 2026) is averaged over each basin, the seasonal cycle is removed, and the trend is tested. Rain trends use GPCP for 2002-2019 only, because we found GPCP drifts dry after 2019 (checked against Kariba's satellite lake level).

3. El Niño fingerprints: rainfall composites with permutation tests show which grids lose water under El Niño. The robust result: 54 GW in 9 grids (including Zambia, Zimbabwe, Vietnam and Peru). Chance alone would give about 2.4 grids.

4. Kariba forecast: G-REALM satellite lake levels since 1992 are converted to % usable storage. A water-balance ensemble built from past El Niño years forecasts the lake 18 months ahead. Kariba rises about 2.1 m less from October to June in El Niño years (p = 0.01).

5. Reservoir watch: the same method, fixed before any crisis was scored, runs on 31 G-REALM reservoirs on 4 continents. It flagged 14 of 17 past hydro crises before they began, 8 of them while the lake was still above its warning level.

6. Proof: Black Marble night lights show the effect of the blackouts: Lusaka dimmed 52% in 2024. Every forecast is hashed and timestamped (SHA-256 and OpenTimestamps), so it can be checked later.

7. Planning: a simulator with an AI assistant lets a user test actions (hold water, imports, rental power, demand cuts, solar) on the 2027 Kariba outlook and see lake level, blackout hours and cost.

WHAT WE REPORT HONESTLY

Our country-level monthly model is weak (Brier skill 0.03-0.07) and is labelled experimental. On the crisis scoreboard, 2 of 5 crises were caught with lead time (Kariba 2024, Vietnam 2023). Brazil 2021, Sichuan 2022 and Ecuador were missed. We also found and documented data problems: breaks in NASA POWER (MERRA-2) rainfall, and GPCP drift after 2019.

BENEFITS

Hydropower droughts are costly. Vietnam's 2023 shortages cost about $1.4 billion (World Bank, preliminary). Ecuador's 2024 blackouts cost about $1.9 billion, about 1.4% of GDP (Banco Central del Ecuador). In Zambia in 2024, power was cut 8, then 12 hours a day. Patronus turns freely available NASA data into a public, early, checkable warning, months ahead instead of weeks. Utilities, river authorities and energy ministries (for example ZESCO, ZPC and the Zambezi River Authority) could use it to plan water releases and imports. Students and the public can use the Trend Detective page to test trends themselves.

GOALS

Give hydro-dependent countries a decision window ("I know how much time I have, and what acting now buys me"), and show the trend evidence in a form anyone can check, misses included.

TOOLS AND LANGUAGES

Python (pandas, numpy, scipy, xarray, netCDF4, h5netcdf, geopandas, shapely, pyogrio, pymannkendall, statsmodels, LightGBM, scikit-learn, requests, Pillow, opentimestamps-client). TypeScript, React and Vite for the site, with d3, topojson-client, world-atlas, three.js and @react-three/fiber for maps and the 3-D globe. Cloudflare Workers to host the site and the assistant endpoint. Remotion for the video. Git and GitHub.
